title: Minimum Wage Australia 18 Year-Old: Hourly to Annual Pay Guide
description: Learn how to convert the minimum wage australia 18 year-old hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay. Includes tax, super, and award comparisons.
salarySummary: Based on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is approximately $52,289.44.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage for an 18 year-old in Australia?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour applies to most adult employees. For 18 year-olds, award rates may be lower depending on the industry and classification. Check the relevant award or the Fair Work Ombudsman for junior rates.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to the minimum wage?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% on top of the base hourly rate. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for entitlements like paid leave. Always enter your base rate without loading in the timesheet.

faqs.q: How do I calculate annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by hours per week (usually 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,289.44 per year. This assumes consistent hours and no overtime.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly to Annual: The Basics

If you earn an hourly wage or are considering a salary offer, the standard formula to estimate annual pay is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For full-time employees, the typical week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. Using this assumption gives a consistent baseline for comparing hourly and annual figures.

For example, the **minimum wage australia 18 year-old** often refers to the adult National Minimum Wage, which from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. On a 38-hour week, that works out to:
- Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.90
- Fortnightly: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80
- Annual: $1,004.90 × 52 = $52,289.44

These figures are gross—before tax and other deductions. The [timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and see these conversions instantly.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

Australia’s pay system has two main layers: the **National Minimum Wage** (set by the Fair Work Commission) and **award rates** (industry-specific minimums set by the Fair Work Ombudsman). The National Minimum Wage applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. For most adult employees, this is the legal floor. However, many workers are covered by an award that may set higher minimum rates for their classification.

When searching for the **minimum wage australia 18 year-old**, note that junior rates under awards are often a percentage of the adult rate. The National Minimum Wage itself does not have a junior rate—it applies to all employees 21 and over. For 18 year-olds, the applicable minimum depends on the award. For example, the General Retail Industry Award might set a rate of $18.50 per hour for a Level 1 employee aged 18. Always check the specific award or use the [pay guides](/blog) to find the correct figure. The [reference tables](/data) on this site summarise common award classifications.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of their base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (annual leave, sick leave). For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). **Important:** When using the [timesheet](/), enter your base hourly rate without casual loading. The checkbox on the timesheet adds the 25% loading automatically. Never enter a rate that already includes loading.

Superannuation (super) is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your pay—it is an additional contribution your employer makes. For example, on the National Minimum Wage annual gross of $52,289.44, the super contribution would be $6,274.73 (12% of $52,289.44). This is an estimate; actual super may vary if you earn above the cap or have salary sacrifice arrangements. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on your taxable income and the tax rates for the 2026–27 financial year. The Australian Taxation Office uses a progressive tax scale:
- $0 – $18,200: nil tax
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on the excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: 45% on the excess over $190,000

Additionally, most residents pay a Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage ($52,289.44), the estimated tax would be approximately $7,033 (including Medicare). This is an estimate only—your actual tax may differ if you have deductions, offsets, or other income. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more personalised calculation.

## Using the Timesheet and Other Tools

The [timesheet](/) is the home page of this site. Enter your base hourly rate, select whether you are casual (to add loading), and the tool will show your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay. It also provides an estimate of tax and super. Remember that the annual figure assumes a 38-hour week for 52 weeks. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

For more detailed comparisons, explore the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page, which uses Australian Bureau of Statistics data. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page explains how to convert salary offers to hourly rates. If you are covered by an award, check the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) and [job pay](/topics/job-pay) pages for specific rates.

## Important Disclaimer

The calculations on this site are estimates. They assume the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold and the 2025–26 Medicare reduction thresholds. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is not a determination of your pay or tax. Always consult a qualified professional for your specific situation.
